rows.author: F100
rows.title_full: RIGHTS OF THE URBAN POOR
rows.abstract: Talked about the plight of the urban poor living in Pangarap Village who were being harassed and threatened with demolition by the Carmel Development, Inc. (CDI), headed by Mr. Greggy Araneta that was claiming ownership of the land lots in said locality. Claimed that the late Pres. Marcos awarded said lots to the present residents. Also narrated the developments on the case filed by the OSG to revoke the ownership titles of CDI to said lots. Said that the case has been pending with the Supreme Court after the OSG filed a motion for reconsideration when the high tribunal ruled in favor of CDI. Condemned what was happening at Pangarap Village, opined that the Araneta Group of Companies and the CDI should follow due process, and sought the help of his colleagues for the sake of the residents.
rows.status: Change of committee referral requested on 2011-08-09
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Malapitan. Referred to the appropriate committee.

committee_action.action: Change of committee referral requested on 2011-08-09

rows.title_full: ISSUES ON THE LEGALITY OF THE AUTOMATED ELECTIONS LAST MAY 2010
rows.abstract:
Held that the May 10, 2010 election that the Comelec had conducted was illegal, irregular and constitutionally infirm. Explained that it did not comply with RA No. 9369 and other pertinent laws regarding the use of an automated election system. Alleged that Comelec officials were aware of their violations. Maintained however that the legal character of the positions held by those who ran and won in the elections fall under the de facto doctrine and that their acts were considered valid, lawful and legally unassailable. Called for an immediate
investigation on the matter not only to determine
the responsibility and culpability of Comelec officials but to see to it that the Constitution and the rule of law would not be violated again.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2011-05-10
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Cagas, Barzaga, Lagman and Nograles. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2011-05-17

rows.author: G062
rows.title_full: NEW POLICIES OF THE PHILIPPINE HEART CENTER FOR CHARITY PATIENTS
rows.title_short: Policies And Guidelines Of Government - Owned - And - Controlled Corporations ( G O C C ) Hospitals
rows.abstract: TALKED ABOUT THE CASE OF CYRUS AQUINO WHO HAS BEEN CONFINED AT THE PHILIPPINE HEART CENTER (PHC). SAID THAT THE BUDGET CUT POLICY OF THE PHC IN 2011 HAD CHANGED COVERING INDIGENT PATIENTS AND PASSED THE BURDEN OF ITS HIGH OPERATING EXPENSES TO THESE PATIENTS. URGED CONGRESS TO CONDUCT A THROUGH ASSESSMENT OF THE OPERATION OF ALL GOVERNMENT-OWNED HOSPITALS PARTICULARLY THE GUIDELINES AND POLICIES BEING IMPLEMENTED FOR INDIGENT PATIENTS SO THAT THE POOREST OF THE POOR WILL NOT BE DEPRIVED OF THE HEALTH SERVICES THEY DESERVE.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2011-05-24

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: RIGHTS OF LESBIANS, GAYS, BISEXUALS AND TRANS-GENDERS (LGBTs)
rows.title_short: International Day Against Homophobia And Transphobia
rows.abstract: TOOK THE FLOOR IN BEHALF OF THE MEMBERS' LESBIAN, GAY, BISEXUAL AND TRANSGENDER (LGBT) CONSTITUENTS.  SAID THAT THE WORLD HEALTH ORGANIZATION REMOVED HOMOSEXUALITY FROM ITS INTERNATIONAL CLASSIFICATION OF MENTAL DISORDERS ON MAY 17, 1990.  UNDERSCORED THAT IDAHO ALSO URGES EVERYONE TO AGGRESSIVELY COMBAT AND OPENLY CONDEMN SEXUAL AND GENDER DISCRIMINATION AND VIOLENCE.  APPEALED FOR THE IMMEDIATE PASSAGE OF HB1483 - ANTI-DISCRIMINATION ACT WHICH AIMS TO ELIMINATE DISCRIMINATION BASED ON SEX, SEXUAL ORIENTATION AND GENDER IDENTITY.  DISCLOSED THAT HE WOULD ALSO FILE A BILL THAT WOULD MAKE MAY 17 AN INTERNATIONAL DAY AGAINST HOMOPHOBIA AND TRANSPHOBIA, ENJOINED HIS COLLEAGUES TO FIGHT FOR THE RIGHTS OF THE LGBTs.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HUMAN RIGHTS since 2011-05-24

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: THE PRESENT OIL CRISIS AS AGGRAVATING FACTOR IN THE COUNTRY'S ECONOMIC CRISIS
rows.abstract:
Focused on the economic issues besetting the present Administration; noted the rapid rise in the prices of oil and food products despite the prevailing high economic growth rate; observed that while the government could not do much to control the rise in prices, a noninterventionist strategy would be a political suicide; cautioned that any sense of fatalism, should be rejected by the President and recommended a comprehensive
strategy to tackle the root cause of the oil crisis, which included the basic wage hike and targeted subsidies, eliminating the imposition of value-added tax on oil products and allowing a flexible price management. Pointed out that 
programs which combine subsidies and tax reductions with mechanisms to moderate the rise in oil prices would significantly slow down the erosion of the people´s living standards and would allow households and companies to rationally plan their production and consumption. Stated however that even if said
programs would not harm the interest of the major
oil companies, the latter might disagree with
the proposed mechanisms; hence, the government
should exercise its political will.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECONOMIC AFFAIRS since 2011-05-24

rows.author: F103
rows.title_full: GOVERNMENT'S PROGRAM FOR AGRICULTURAL DEVELOPMENT
rows.abstract: SPOKE ON THE PLIGHT OF THE FARMERS AND FISHERFOLKS WHO CONTINUE TO REMAIN IMPOVERISHED EVEN THOUGH THEY ARE THE ONES WHO PRODUCED FOOD FOR THE COUNTRY. NOTED THAT THE GOVERNMENT HAS CONTINUED TO IGNORE THESE DIFFICULTIES EVEN AS AGRICULTURE REMAINS THE DEVELOPMENT BACKBONE OF THE COUNTRY AND THAT THE GOVERNMENT SHOULD INCREASE THEIR PRODUCTIVITY TO ADDRESS THE PROBLEM OF RURAL POVERTY. CALLED ON CONGRESS TO PUSH FOR A MORE RESPONSIVE BUDGET ALLOCATION FOR AGRICULTURE; STRENGTHEN GOVERNMENT INSTITUTIONS THAT PROVIDE FINANCIAL SUPPORT TO THE FARMERS; AND UNDERTAKE MEASURES TO HAVE A BETTER GRASP OF THE MAGNITUDE OF ILLEGAL LAND USE CONVERSION.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2011-05-24

POINTED OUT THAT IT WAS BOTH INCORRECT AND INAPPROPRIATE TO ASSUME THAT THE JUSTICES ARE VIRTUALLY CLOTHED WITH IMMUNITY EVEN IF THEY ARE ENTITLED TO PUBLIC TRUST BECAUSE THE JUSTICES... ARE IMPEACHABLE.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-05-18)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep.Fua. Referred to the Committee on Justice.

rows.author: C128
rows.title_full: CONCERNS OF AGRARIAN REFORM BENEFICIARIES
rows.abstract:
Talked about the development of agrarian reform beneficiaries (ARBs) as they are vital to sound and sustainable rural development.  Expressed
concern about the future of ARBs at the end of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP)
in 2014.  Suggested : (1) private-public partnership projects; (2) socialized credit windows; (3) irrigation systems, farmto-
market roads, and housing projects; (4) funds for subsidized credit; and (5) the amendment of IRR of R.A. No. 9700.  Asked the Congressional
Oversight Committee on Agrarian Reform to immediately tackle said issues and the President to promulgate an EO providing for an integrated
policy on support services delivery.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2011-05-31

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: RE-EVALUATION OF THE EFFECTS OF THE OPERATION OF COAL MINING AND COAL-FIRED POWER PLANTS PARTICULARLY ON THE HEALTH OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN
rows.abstract: Took the floor in observance of the 24th International Day of Action for Women´s Health. Stressed the government´s program of promoting the use of coal-fired power plants to address the problem of energy supply, and explained why the use of coal poses major environmental and health hazards.  Cited studies from different organizations such as the WHO and the UN Environment Program, which confirmed the adverse effects of coal mining on humans and on the entire planet earth. Emphasized the ill effects of coal production on the reproductive health of women and underscored that the advantages of coal as declared by the DOE and other mining groups are simply outmatched by its disadvantages and ill-effects on society and environment. Called on her colleagues and the House leadership to reexamine the country´s national policy on coal mining and coal-fired power plants.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2011-05-31
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Apostol, Cagas, Aumentado. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G088
rows.title_full: TRIAL BY JURY IN OUR CRIMINAL JUSTICE SYSTEM
rows.abstract:
Relayed the events surrounding the assassination of his friend, former Puerto Princesa
City Vice Mayor Fernando “Dong” Batul, and trial of the accused gunman. Opined that the accused
should have been convicted rather than acquitted. Suggested the adoption of a system of trial by jury in criminal cases, and enjoined his colleagues to support the passage of a measure allowing the outcome of criminal trials less dependent on the subjective dispositions of the judges and more satisfactory to the public.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on JUSTICE since 2011-05-31
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Payuyo.  Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: RIGHTS AND WELFARE OF MIGRANT DOMESTIC WORKERS
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body that parliamentarians
from Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, Sri Lanka
and the Philippines were set to forge an alliance of labor exporting countries which were committed to defend the rights and welfare of domestic workers. Said that Akbayan Party-List had proposed a twotrack strategy that Congress and its foreign counterparts must take: engage processes that create an international framework for decent work for domestic workers; and develop policies on national migration to ensure the effective implementation of existing
ones.  Emphasized the need for parliamentarians
from the aforesaid Asian countries to form a strong alliance to ensure the protection of the
rights of their migrant workers; facilitate cooperation and easier exchange of information among them; and set the tone for discussions of the prospects of a Southeast Asian framework for the protection of migrant workers´ rights that could be included in the agenda of the coming ASEAN Inter-Parliamentary Assembly.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on OVERSEAS WORKERS AFFAIRS since 2011-05-31

rows.author: F115
rows.title_full: ON INDIVIDUALS AND GROUPS WHO REPRESENT THEMSELVES AS MEMBERS OF THE SENIOR CITIZENS PARTY LIST TO THE COMELEC
rows.title_short: Disqualification Case Against Senior Citizens Partylist Rep. Dennis Kho And Petition To Amend The Partylist's Name
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the alleged maneuverings to disqualify Rep. David L. Kho as the 2nd Representative
of the Party-List Coalition of Senior Citizens in the Philippines, Inc. and to replace the latter with Mr. Francisco Gambao Datol Jr. who Rep. Arquiza described as a self-proclaimed political strategist and Comelec “operator” and who, coincidentally, was the third nominee of their Party-List. Narrated the details surrounding said maneuverings and concluded that there was a well-planned move to seat Mr. Datol at all cost and ahead of the latter´s term-sharing agreement with Rep.
Kho. Alleged that Mr. Datol and his
group had 1) continued attacking the Party-List organization; 2) asked the SEC to investigate and declare their organization illegal; 3) filed an association similar to the name of their Party-List, and which the SEC had approved;
4) filed a baseless case against him without
any supporting documents or evidence; and 5) wanted to disqualify Rep. Kho to allow their nominee to take his place, among others. Further disclosed that the Comelec had given due course to alleged fake and falsified documents seeking a change in name of Rep. Arquiza´s Party-List group. Opined that the Comelec scalawags should be exposed. Asked the President, to lead them in cleansing the Commission of remnants of corruption.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2011-07-26

rows.author: G118
rows.title_full: ON THE ISSUES DISCUSSED DURING THE 8TH REGIONAL WOMEN MINISTERS' AND PARLIAMENTARIANS'CONFERENCE ON YOUNG WOMEN AND GIRLS
rows.abstract:
Spoke about the 8th Regional Women Ministers´ and Parliamentarians´ Conference on Young Women and Girls held in Jakarta, Indonesia. Said that the Conference evolved around the themes of enhancing parliamentary support amongst parliamentarians from the Asia-Pacific
region, and monitoring the promotion of gender
equality and women empowerment. Pointed out that while Filipino women left an indelible mark in Philippine politics and education, the Jakarta Conference however reported that the country still suffered poorly in some aspects of gender equality and women health care. Proposed several structural reforms, among which are the amendments to the Labor Code that will broaden the scope of acts of discrimination against women and the legislative review and passage of other legislative measures pertaining to women´s rights. Maintained that the benefits of women empowerment also impact on men and children and the whole Filipino society. Further claimed that women empowerment could be achieved through the enactment of appropriate laws addressing violence, poverty, inequality and discrimination against women.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WOMEN AND GENDER EQUALITY since 2011-07-26

rows.author: F100
rows.title_full: ANOMALIES IN THE USE OF THE CHARITY FUND OF THE PCSO
rows.title_short: Alleged Misuse Of P C S O Funds
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body of the story of a woman stricken with breast cancer and who subsequently died after failing to get medical assistance
from the (PCSO) to underscore the need for Congress to look into the agency´s misuse of billions of public funds. Claimed that the profligate waste of public funds allegedly
resulted from anomalous transactions during
the previous Administration wherein the PCSO had
“comingled” and diverted the sales proceeds from its lotto operations to fund anomalous contracts for advertising and public relations. Disclosed certain anomalous transactions of the PCSO, which included the purchase of overpriced small-town lotto (STL) handheld machines and the anomalous diversion of P150M in PR funds to intelligence funds. Called on his colleagues
for an immediate investigation of the PCSO alleged anomalous activities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2011-07-26

rows.author: F104
rows.title_full: ON THE PRESSING PROBLEMS IN THE EDUCATION SYSTEM OF THE COUNTRY
rows.abstract:
Expressed his concern on the chaotic condition of the Philippine education system and the Filipino youth´s apparent lack of access to educational opportunities. Opined that the education crisis was rooted in an insufficient budget. Criticized programs such as the K-12 plan which seeks to increase the elementary-to-secondary school cycle to rapidly generate employable graduates to fill in the demands of the foreign market. Lamented the high tuition fees in private tertiary institutions
and the government neglect of their public counterparts. Concluded that the government must review its policies and implement political solutions as regards education.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2011-07-26

rows.author: G009
rows.title_full: ON THE NEED TO INSTITUTE REFORMS IN THE AQUACULTURE AND FISHERIES SECTOR
rows.abstract:
Discussed the problems besetting the fisheries sector namely: the rapid depletion of fish stock caused by destructive practices, poverty, and tenurial insecurity due to the privatization and commercialization of fishing grounds. Advocated the NGOs for Fisheries Reform Coalition´s recommendations such as the passage of the National Land Use and Management Act and the funding of the 25-year Comprehensive National Fishery Industry Development Plan, the government declaration of foreshore areas,
buffer zones and salvage zones as public domains, a thorough assessment of the implementation of the Fisheries Code of 1998, and the implementation of a strategic poverty-alleviation program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AQUACULTURE AND FISHERIES RESOURCES since 2011-07-26

rows.author: F071
rows.title_full: ON THE STRINGENT PROCEUDRE OF ORGAN DONATION BY INMATES OF THE NATIONAL BILIBID PRISON
rows.abstract:
Rose to convey the story of a constituent of his whose kidney transplant did not materialize because the kidney donor happened to be an inmate at the National Bilibid Prisons. Lamented that the DOJ had denied his request to facilitate the kidney donation citing provisions
from the Bureau of Corrections Manual and the
rampant selling of organs in jailhouses.
Called the attention of Congress to rectify the matter as he expressed belief that a person´s
right to save lives should not be taken away
even if he/she is a convict.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2011-07-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.abstract:
Informed the Body that a memorandum issued by the regional director of the Philippine Postal Corporation (NCR) and a Philpost Circular had undermined the franking privilege enjoyed by
the Members of the House of Representatives under RA No.6650. Underscored that the Philpost issuances had caused undue delays and were also a
form of censorship which was contrary to RA No.
6650, and Article III of the Constitution, regarding the privacy of communications and correspondence. Pointing out that imposing strict measures on their franking privilege seemed a desperate attempt of Philpost to raise revenues, he then inquired into the present financial status of Philpost and asked whether its income losses were due to some lapses in
its leadership and/or management.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-05-31)
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G064
rows.title_full: HIS RESPONSE TO THE SMEARING OF HIS PERSON BECAUSE OF BEING ANTI-RH BILL
rows.title_short: Alleged Smear Campaign Against Him Being An Anti - R H Bill.
rows.abstract:
Castigated what he called an elaborate plot to destroy his reputation and those of other anti-RH Bill Members and read into the records the
contents of a micro-blogging site calling for a smear campaign against him in Davao City. Said that he would name names, file the pertinent suits, and ask for a congressional inquiry at the appropriate time as who was funding the campaign, where were the funds coming from, how big the people involved and what were their motives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2011-07-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bag-ao. Manifestation by Rep. Marcoleta. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.title_full: HIS RESPONSE TO AN ARTICLE ON THE MAY 26 ISSUE OF THE PHIL. DAILY INQUIRER RE:  PLENARY DEBATES OF THE REPRODUCTIVE HEALTH BILL
rows.title_short: His Position On The R H Bill.
rows.abstract:
Described as uncomplimentary, premeditated
and malicious the statements made by Rep. Edcel C. Lagman that his questions on the RH Bill in general and about God and U.S. imperialism in particular, were repetitive and irrelevant.  Cited the Supreme Court decision in the case of American Bible Society vs. The City of Manila as he pointed out that the issue of religion cannot be discussed without including God in the discussion. Also stated that his questions on US imperialism was a valid issue because the RH Bill was inspired by the American government and funding institutions to serve the security and strategic interests of the US. Furthermore, Garcia said that he had cautioned the Sponsor against answering his questions regarding the latter´s connection with the PLCPD because of a possible conflict of interest under Section 12, Article VI of the Constitution.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2011-07-26
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.title_full: ON THE IRREGULARITIES IN THE BIR OFFICE IN ORIENTAL MINDORO
rows.title_short: Irregularities In The Bureau Of Internal Revenue ( B I R )
rows.abstract:
Called the attention of the Body to the irregularities allegedly being perpetuated by certain officials of the BIR against ordinary businessmen and professionals in Oriental Mindoro, specifically the refusal of RDO No.63 to release certificates of tax exemption to several qualified cooperatives to the detriment of their economic operations. Added that the Calapan City Federation of Cooperatives and
the Calapan Labor Service Development Cooperative
had brought their plight to his attention. He then called on the BIR Commissioner and its top officials to conduct an immediate investigation on the complaint of said cooperatives against the BIR officials concerned and to file the necessary preventive suspension in the course of their investigation.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WAYS AND MEANS since 2011-07-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Garcia(P) and Ping-ay. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F035
rows.title_full: ON THE ERRORS IN THE AWARDS OF CONTRACTS IN THE AFP
rows.title_short: Awarding Of Armed Forces Of The Philippines ( A F P ) Contracts
rows.abstract:
Expressed apprehension over some erroneous contracts awarded by the Bids and Awards Committee of the Department of National
Defense, in order to favor bidders who
peddle inferior and oversized equipment in utter disregard for the lives and limbs of the men and women of the AFP. Mentioned that among such contracts awarded in the course of implementing the AFP Modernization Program was the P60-million project for the purchase of UHF base and handheld radios and integrated logistics
support for the Philippine Army. Emphasized the major role of the Government Procurement Policy Board (GPPB) in the procurement process, referred to the provisions of the Government Procurement Reform Act pertaining to BACs and transparency in the bidding process, and lamented how the DND-BAC had abused its mandate under the law and had favored anointed bidders.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL DEFENSE AND SECURITY since 2011-07-26

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: ACQUISITION OF DIGITEL BY PLDT-SMART
rows.abstract:
Rose to protect the integrity of the House and help prevent the re-emergence of a monopoly in the telecommunications industry with the recent purchase by PLDT Company, owner of Smart Communications, Inc., of Digitel Telecommunications, Inc. which owned Sun Cellular. Recalled PLDT´s monopolized the telecommunications industry several years ago and how the Constitution had abhorred the existence of monopolies while franchise laws had provided built-in safeguards against the unintended reconsolidation of the industry. Raised several concerns: 1) PLDT-Smart had gained control of 71% of the telecommunications industry; 2) the country´s top three telecommunications companies (telcos) namely PLDT, Digitel, and Globe had to secure congressional approval first before undertaking any lease, transfer, grant of usufruct, sale and transfer of rights and privileges of their franchises; 3) the PLDT-Digitel merger was illegal as it was done without any
congressional approval and would only foster
monopoly; and 4) the NTC cannot be expected to protect the interest of the consumers because its commissioners were allegedly on the payroll of the telcos. Concluded that Congress should not allow PLDT-Digitel from monopolizing the industry, and cautioned the NTC and the SEC against approving the merger.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LEGISLATIVE FRANCHISES since 2011-10-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Apostol. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F086
rows.title_full: ON THE ISSUANCE OF SPECIAL ALLOTMENT (SARO)
rows.title_short: Power Of The Purse Of Congress
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body of the various laws and Constitutions that had become the basis for
the “power of the purse” of Congress more particularly of the House of Representatives and which power had been repeatedly emasculated by the Executive Department through the nonissuance by DBM of SAROs and NCAs to implement the
so-called pork barrel allocations of the Members. Also discussed how the pork barrel allocations had been institutionalized in the yearly appropriation of public funds; expounded on the specific procedures on how these allocations were provided to each Member of Congress; and cited the Supreme Court´s
recognition of the legality of pork barrel allocations in the case of PHILCONSA vs. Enriquez, et al. Expressed his sentiments on what he perceived as a deliberate delay on the part of DBM to release the SAROs and wondered who could address the dire need for funds of their respective districts. Called on his colleagues not to allow this kind of practice
and said that this was the reason why he filed House Bill No. 4296 to strengthen the Legislature´s power of the purse.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2011-07-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Padilla. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G010
rows.title_full: IMPACT OF MINING ON INDIGENOUS COMMUNITIES
rows.abstract:
Focused on the various violations against the civil, political and collective rights of indigenous Filipinos, particularly in the implementation of the principle of free, prior and informed consent (FPIC), as mandated under the Indigenous Peoples Rights Act (IPRA) of 1997, in consultation processes involving mining applications and the adverse effects of mining to indigenous communities. Advanced the following recommendations: 1) for the
Members to act on the consolidation of the three
mining bills; 2) for the President to issue an executive order calling for a moratorium on mining activities while the government´s national mining policy was being improved; and 3) for the Executive Branch to conduct an investigation on the impact of mining vis-Ã -vis its contribution to the country´s economy as well as an inquiry into mining-related killings in order to prosecute the guilty.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-07-26

rows.author: G093
rows.title_full: DEFICIENCIES IN THE EDUCATION SYSTEM IN THE COUNTRY
rows.title_short: Shortage Of Classrooms And Teachers And Of K12
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the perennial problem of the shortage in regular teachers, classrooms, chairs and toilets in the public school sector during school opening which the Aquino Administration had failed to address. Focused his speech on President Aquino´s K-12 education reform program particularly the universal kindergarten education program, and disclosed that the DepEd recent issuance of DepEd Order No. 37 to address the problem on the shortage of teachers for kindergarten was illegal and in violation of RA No. 7836 or the Philippine Teachers Professionalization Act of 1994 because it encouraged the deployment in public schools of unlicensed, volunteer kindergarten teachers.
Suggested that the Executive Branch and
Congress work hand in hand to pass a supplemental
budget needed for the implementation of the universal kindergarten education program. Likewise called on the Committee on Basic Education and Culture to investigate the preparedness of DepEd in implementing said program for school year 2011-2012.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HIGHER AND TECHNICAL EDUCATION since 2011-07-26

rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: PROPOSED TO DECLARE \"BAYBAYIN\" AS THE NATIONAL SCRIPT OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Re : House Bill 4395 Baybayin As National Script ( Alibata )
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bataoil initially pointed out that his speech about the preservation and conservation of a nearly forgotten part of Filipino cultural heritage and national identity - the early Filipino syllabary called baybayin or alibata which means “to spell”- was timely and significant because it would complement the objective of the forthcoming celebration of the
150th birth anniversary of Dr. Jose Rizal which was to promote and protect Philippine heritage.
He informed the Body that to preserve a Philippine treasure and out of his sense of nationalism and patriotism, he had filed House Bill No. 4395 to protect and conserve the use of baybayin and to declare the Filipino syllabary as the national script of the Philippines. He claimed that the revival of baybayin as part of the country´s cultural heritage would contribute
to the country´s national identity and search
for unity. He then urged the Members to expedite the enactment into law of said measure.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2011-07-26

rows.author: C047
rows.title_full: PROTESTED TO THE PROPOSED CREATION OF THE PROVINCE OF NUEVA CAMARINES
rows.title_short: Opposing The Creation Of The Province Of Nueva Camarines As Contained In House Bill No. 4728.
rows.abstract:
Underscored his objection to HB No. 4728, creating a new province of Nueva Camarines
to include the 4th and 5th legislative districts of Camarines Sur. Claimed that the author of the
measure, Deputy Speaker Fuentebella, had failed to accord him the appropriate courtesy as the Representative of the 5th District by filing a measure without seeking his opinion and the approval of his constituents on a very important matter. Stressed that the opinion of his constituents was paramount in the consideration of the proposed province of Nueva Camarines.
Said that the Rep. Fuentebella should not have included his district without his consent, should have at least followed the Rules of the House, and should have accorded him parliamentary courtesy. Asked that his district be removed from the coverage of said House Bill.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2011-07-26

rows.author: A036
rows.title_full: RESPONSE TO REP. FORTUNO'S SPEECH AGAINST THE CREATION OF THE PROVINCE OF NUEVA CAMARINES
rows.title_short: Re:  Response On The Speech Of Hon. Fortuno On The Creation Of The Province Of Nueva Camarines
rows.abstract: Pointed out that under the Rules, a Member has to consult another if the nature of the bill he or she had filed would affect the other´s distric. Said that a Member could file a bill of general nature which would affect the welfare of the Filipino people and without consultation with another Member if it would not affect any particular district especially if there were no boundaries to speak of. Explained how HB No. 4728 was publicized in the local media and how certain barangay and municipal officials in his district rooted for the Bill when they discussed the prospects of their district´s development as well as belabored the fact that their district alone was much bigger in terms of land area and population compared to eight other provinces. Advised Rep. Fortuno that the creation of a province follows several legislative and legal procedures which include the conduct of a plebiscite. Said that Members generally file bills with the entire country´s welfare in mind, have the prerogative to file what measures they want to file, and should stand up independently in representation of their constituencies. Stressed that resource persons had already affirmed the Bill´s compliance with the income, population, and land area requirements of the Local Government Code.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2011-07-26

rows.author: G095
rows.title_short: Philippine Long Distance Telephone Company ( P L D T )- Digitel
