rows.author: G042
rows.title_full: FOREIGN POLICY ON THE SPRATLY ISLANDS DISPUTE
rows.abstract:
Said that the overlapping claims in the South China Sea in general and Spratlys Islands
in particular threatened historical comity and
solidarity in Southeast Asia. Discussed the relevance of the South China Sea to the region in terms of trade, security, and the development of new energy resources. To protect the national interest, he then proposed the following: (1) a forceful and consistent congressional advocacy for the peaceful management and desirable resolution of the Spratlys conflict; (2) a
congressional inquiry on the Philippines´ legal claim, military requirements to maintain a credible presence in the Kalayaan Islands, and diplomatic efforts; (3) the forging of a national strategy and policy on a negotiated
settlement of the claims; (4) a diplomatic,
bilateral, regional and international approach to the issue; (5) a review of the RP-US Mutual Defense Treaty and RP-China Bilateral Code of Conduct; and (6) the consideration of various other strategies in resolving the issue as suggested by private analysts and presidents of the Association of South East Asian Nations
(ASEAN) member-countries.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2011-07-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Golez (R). Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F034
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATING THE MOUNT PINATUBO ERUPTION
rows.abstract:
Mount Pinatubo eruption left its devastating effects in the Province of Pampanga, the Pampangueños had managed to survive the overwhelming natural catastrophe and the threat of lahar because of their steadfast and resilient resolve as well as with the help of former Presidents Corazon C. Aquino and Fidel V. Ramos, and numerous elected public officials.
Rep. Gonzales cited the reasons why the Municipality of Bacolor had remained wanting of full recovery and rehabilitation; the initiatives he had taken to address this concern, which included the enactment of the Bacolor Rehabilitation Act; the absence of definite funding sources for the implementation of said Act; the commemorative activities on June 15 to mark the 20th anniversary of the Mt. Pinatubo eruption; and the need of Bacolor townspeople for congressional support to be able to rise and chart a new future.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2011-07-26

rows.author: E032
rows.title_full: ON THER STAND AGAINST ABORTION
rows.title_short: Her Being A Doctor And A Legislator
rows.abstract: Argued on the need to clarify the issues and misconceptions regarding the use of contraceptives such as pills and condoms and to compare their usage to Viagra and other erectile dysfunction medicines. Underscored why condoms and birth control pills were demonized and rejected in Phil. society when these should have been regarded as life-saving medical devices, how the use of Viagra and similar medicines gained wide acceptance and led to a bias against the use of contraceptives, and why there was no conclusive link between breast cancer and pills among women. Likewise expounded on other issues: the methods and guidelines which doctors use to determine whether a couple needs contraception or not; the need to deal with the issue of RH Bill in a mature and responsible manner; the side effects of medicines; her anti-abortion stance; how doctors are sometimes constrained by technology but on many occasions bound by medical ethics; her appeal for all concerned to accord the doctors with due respect; and the lack of conspiracy among doctors, RH advocates, pharmaceutical companies and foreign governments in promoting reproductive health in the Philippines.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2011-07-26

rows.author: G064
rows.title_full: HEALTH RISKS OF CONTRACEPTIVES
rows.title_short: Department Of Health And Food And Drugs Administration
rows.abstract:
Stressed that the DOH and FDA failed to implement the provisions of the Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act and the Consumer Act of the Philippines to protect and promote maternal health. Explained that certain pills and devices such as the “morning-after pill,” IUDs
and manual vacuum aspirator were found by the USFDA and American federal courts, pill manufacturers, and research institutes, to prevent the implantation of the fertilized egg and to result in heart attack, stroke, and cancer. Cited studies showing that said drugs prevent ovulation, fertilization and implantation
and have estrogen and progesterone content with
abortifacient action. Citing Republic Act No. 5921 which prohibits the sale of drugs, chemical product or device capable of provoking abortion or preventing conception to any person without prescription, he lamented that the reality was that contraceptive pills could be purchased
by any person over the counter, regardless of
age, sex or civil status. Asked why the government had allowed such hazardous drugs and devices to be openly sold and distributed in the country. Called on Congress to immediately
investigate the serious failure of government
health agencies to defend and safeguard the health of the Filipino people, particularly the women, in accordance with the letter, spirit and intent of the law.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2011-07-26
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Lagman. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.abstract:
Initially pointed out the President´s use of symbols such as wang-wang to show the gvernment´s probity in good governance. Stressed however that the presidency must be above symbols as the government should pursue concrete plans and viable visions to achieve national growth and development. Delved on the failure of the President to follow through on the 3-pronged agenda of his 2010 SONA, to wit: 1) the legislative priorities requiring the enactment of 7 priority measures; 2) an economic agenda to be pursued through a PPPs strategy; and 3) a governance centerpiece agenda against corruption. Pointed out the uneven treatment of Members of Congress with respect to the releases of their respective allocations under the PDAF. Observed that consequently, economic growth slowed down in the 1st quarter of 2011 while other standard economic indicators remained
bleak. Noted that President Aquino failed to disclose his government´s labor plans and his inaction on the agrarian case in Hacienda Luisita. Criticized the government´s expansion
of its CCT program which he said was not a comprehensive approach to poverty alleviation and was not sustainable because it was a mere dole-out. Spoke about the pending measures which sought to criminalize enforced disappearance as a separate offense and observed the absence of a human rights agenda in President Aquino´s latest SONA. Noted the President´s lack of reference in his speech to the Reproductive Health Bill despite his steadfast advocacy of responsible parenthood and surmised that the Chief Executice wanted to prevent a further widening of the chasm between his Administration and the Catholic Church. Warned that what might remain at the end of the day is the presidential wang-wang of “3Ps” or promises, propaganda and palliatives.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-08-16

rows.author: B006
rows.title_full: ON PRESIDENT'S AQUINO'S PEACE NEGOTIATIONS WITH THE MILF
rows.title_short: Meeting Of Pnoy With Milf Leadership
rows.abstract:
Expressed his deepest gratitude to Pres. Benigno S. Aquino III for initiating the historic meeting
with MILF leader Al Haj Murad Ibrahim which took place in Tokyo, Japan and which was the first between a head of state and the MILF since the intermittent peace talks started 14 years ago.
Disclosed that the peace talk revived the interest and trust of the Muslim people in the Aquino government´s goodwill and ability to kick-start peace negotiations and expressed hope that it would continue until a final peace agreement is reached. Pointed out that peace should be measured against standards of nutrition, education and selfgovernment and expressed hope that the MILF would join the government in the difficult and complex task of achieving peace for Mindanao.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.title_full: ON THE ALLEGED SACRILEGIOUS ART EXHIBIT AT THE CULTURAL CENTER OF THE PHILIPPINES
rows.title_short: Obscene Art Exhibit In Cultural Center Of The Philippines
rows.abstract:
Rose on a question of personal privilege
regarding what he called an obscene art exhibit of images of Jesus Christ at the Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP), which he deemed a direct affront to the entire Christiandom. Condemned the artist concerned and the CCP management for their insensitivity in allowing images of Jesus to be displayed in a rather obscene and vulgar manner and stressed that
inasmuch as the CCP was considered a revered institution in promoting Filipino culture and art, the blasphemous portrayal of Jesus was an apparent disregard for Filipino Christian values.
Informed the Body that he had filed a Resolution asking for the resignation of the CCP officials responsible for the aforementioned religious
irreverence and asked the Body to immediately
act on the matter.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Crisologo and Escudero. Manifestation by Rep. Marcos. Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: A040
rows.title_full: ON THE SPRATLY ISLANDS DISPUTE
rows.title_short: Diplomacy To Resolve Conflicts Over Spratly Islands
rows.abstract:
Presented various maps on how the islands looked like and what their distances were relative to the claimant-countries. Described the Chinese “creeping invasion” such as the 
building of structures thereat, cited the definition of the term exclusive economic zones (EEZs) under the UNCLOS, and explained that the territorial dispute over the islands was rooted in the huge oil potential of the islands.
Quoted the salient points contained in the 2002 Declaration on the Conduct of Parties in the South China Sea which the ASEAN countries and China signed as a result of a Mischief Reef incident and which sought to reduce the threat of war or a military clash in the area. Cited the Mutual Defense Treaty entered into between the Philippines and the US and read in particular Articles IV and V thereof re: any armed attack in the Pacific area against either of the parties, with said area covering the China Sea and the Phil. Sea. Expressed concern over talks that the South China Sea disputes could lead to war and stressed that many countries and major players appeared interested in what is happening in the Spratlys,... Discussed the importance of using state diplomacy, such as elevating the dispute to
the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
(ITLOS), and public diplomacy, including the use of social networking to protest China´s encroachment in the South China Sea, as a two-pronged approach in resolving the Spratlys issue. Reiterated the significance of the Spratly Islands not only in relation to the country´s sovereignty but also to the huge assets
that could be derived from the exploration of the
area that would help prop up the national economic development of the country.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on FOREIGN AFFAIRS since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Bello, Biazon and Aumentado. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E041
rows.title_full: REACTION TO STATEMENTS MADE AGAINST HER BY SEC. CARANDANG PUBLISHED IN A NEWSPAPER
rows.title_short: Sec. Carandang's Attack On Her Person Over Her Allegations Of Overpriced Laptops Purchased By Palace Communications Group
rows.abstract:
Took to task Communications Group Sec. Ricky Carandang for maligning and attacking her person in the August 4, 2011 issue of the Philippine Daily Inquirer re: the forced resignation of Asst. Sec. Reginald Tongol over the procurement of expensive Apple laptop computers. Challenged
Sec. Carandang to disclose all documents
pertaining to the two failed biddings and the
negotiated bidding of Apple laptop computers.
Pointed out that she had every right to question
the purchases made by Sec. Carandang and the members of his communications group, and which she would be doing in the forthcoming budget
hearing on Sec. Carandang´s agency.
rows.status: Consigned to the Archives on 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Rep. Escudero. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G010
rows.title_full: NATIONAL SITUATION OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body that representatives of indigenous peoples (IPs)... celebrate the 17th International Day of the World´s Indigenous Peoples and start off a three-month campaign on IPs rights and empowerment. Explained that the theme of the campaign pertained to the rights and issues of indigenous women and their contributions to society as guardians of the environment, bearers of cultural integrity and heritage, and movers of history. Commented that Pres. Benigno S. Aquino III did not mention in his latest SONA how his government intended to
address the plight of the IPs,.. Mentioned several recommendations categorized under the major IP themes, which were forged during a National IP Summit conducted by the House Committee on National Cultural Communities
in partnership with various civil society
organizations (CSOs).
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Commttee on Rules.

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: SITUATION OF WOMEN INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
rows.abstract:
Articulated the sad plight of indigenous women in the country despite their rights which were guaranteed under the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples and the Phil. Indigenous Peoples Rights Act (IPRA). Disclosed that in a recent national gathering of indigenous women, it was emphasized that indigenous women had long been discriminated against in various ways, such as not being recognized for their knowledge and contributions to the community, being excluded in local and national decision-making processes, and being victims of militarization and human rights abuses. Recommended that her colleagues adopt a House Resolution recognizing the valuable contributions of indigenous women to society as well as conduct congressional inquiries into the 4Ps program and incidents of harassment
involving indigenous women so that the latter may
receive the attention and respect due them.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: A088
rows.title_full: LEGISLATIVE AGENDA FOR INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
rows.abstract:
Advocated the continued protection of indigenous peoples (IPs).. stressed the oppression, abuse, and prejudice that they had suffered throughout history. Cited his constituency´s experience in balancing development and respect for the rights of IPs such as the right to ancestral domain, ... a review of the implementation of the Indigenous Peoples´ Rights Act (IPRA); the recognition of their right to self-determination and role in the peace process; and the protection of their communities from militarization and adverse effects of development. Asked his colleagues to work for the passage of several pending bills
which would advance the well-being of said sector.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G022
rows.title_full: NEED FOR MANDATORY REPRESENTATION OF INDIGENOUS PEOPLES IN LOCAL GOVERNMENT UNITS
rows.abstract:
Delivered her maiden speech... towards the development of the IPs. Noted that the government
had yet to address the material needs of various IP communities,... enjoined her colleagues to
craft policies that will chart better lives for the IPs. Observed that with the signing of the UNDRIP in 2007, the promotion of IP rights had become a global concern with the international
community even calling for more concerted efforts
of governments to respond to the needs and demands of cultural communities. Lamented
that despite enactment, RA No. 8371 or the IPRA has not yet fulfilled its task of addressing the poverty problem among the IPs and enforcing the constitutional mandate of promoting their rights. Cited in particular the mandatory representation of IPs in all local legislative
councils which,... require IP representation whose members would enjoy the same privileges as the regular council members. Asked the 1) National Commission on Indigenous Peoples (NCIP), in coordination with the DILG, to immediately issue the supplement to the Commission´s 2009 National Guideline; 2) Congress, to look into the budget allocation of the NCIP ; and 3) national government agencies and LGUs, to pay attention to the concerns of the IP. Thanked the Speaker for declaring additional priority bills providing for a scholarship program to IPs and creating a center for studies on indigenous cultural communities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Pacquiao. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G029
rows.title_full: THE INDIGENOUS PEOPLES RIGHTS ACT
rows.title_short: Rights Of Indigenous Peoples On Their Ancestral Lands
rows.abstract:
Dwelt on certain provisions of RA No. 8371 or the IPRA, particularly those giving the IPs the right to secure individual certificates of
title for their ancestral lands and creating the Ancestral Domains Special Fund, which he said
should be more vigorously pursued and implemented
to ensure that the rights of the IPs are respected and protected. Recalled how they
welcomed the passage of the IPRA as a milestone
in their socio-economic development for it enhanced peace and development of their communities. Proposed that a P60-million budgetary allocation should be provided in the 2012 GAA as Ancestral Domains Special Fund to facilitate the delineation and titling of ancestral domains and bring about harmonious relations in the cultural communities.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16

rows.author: G009
rows.title_full: MINING AND ITS IMPACT ON INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
rows.title_short: Exploitation Of Indigenous Peoples And Their Ancestral Lands By Mining Companies
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bag-ao brought to the fore the main issue
confronting the country´s indigenous peoples: the
state policy enunciated in the Philippine Mining
Act of 1995 which she said had always been a
source of perennial conflict because the law provided
for the exploitation of the country´s natural
resources in lands inhabited and protected by indigenous
peoples. She explained that the granting
of rights of ownership to ancestral domains by the
State to the IPs, while keeping ownership of natural
resources for exploitation by mining companies,
ultimately marginalizes the livelihood and
existence of the cultural minorities.
With the continued exploitation of the indigenous
peoples resulting in human rights abuses,
environmental disaster and militarization, Rep.
Bag-ao proposed the repeal of the Mining Act and
proposed a new minerals management law that
will prioritize the interests and rights of the IPs
and shall adopt a policy of stewardship which will
preserve and conserve the ancestral lands for future
generations of indigenous peoples.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: MILLENIUM DEVELOPMENT GOALS AND DELIVERY OF SOCIAL SERVICES TO INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
rows.title_short: Education And Health Rights Of Indigenous Peoples
rows.abstract:
Rep. Bataoil focused on various issues related
to education and health rights of the indigenous
peoples of the country. Specifically, he was concerned
for the universal primary education needs
and the indigenization of basic education curriculum
for the benefit of cultural communities considering
that only 70% of the indigenous peoples
are literate, mainly because of the inaccessibility
of education facilities for IPs who live in the remotest
and isolated areas of the country. He also
cited certain problems of the NCIP relative to its
management of the Educational Assistance Program
(EAP). He recommended, among others, to
undertake an in-depth participatory and multidisciplinary
review of the implementation of the
NCIP; monitor closely the NCIP to ensure that it
implements the COA recommendations; and provide
more support for the reinforcement of indigenous
peoples´ education and community schools.
Rep. Bataoil also advanced certain recommendations
to ensure that the health programs and
policies affecting IPs are implemented, including
the need for the NCIP and the Department of
Health to review existing health programs for cultural
minorities, to promote and use indicators developed
on IPs´ wellbeing, and safety of community
health workers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: IMPACT OF MILITARIZATION ON INDIGENOUS PEOPLES
rows.title_short: Human Rights Violation On Indigenous Peoples
rows.abstract:
Rep. Casiño asked that his speech, which cited
several instances of human rights violations by
state security forces tasked to implement largescale
mining and development projects, be inserted
into the Record of the House. Expressing support
for IPs, he recommended the study and implementation
of an IP agenda submitted by various groups
to President Aquino in August 2010; the withdrawal
of military/paramilitary troops and imposition
of a moratorium on large-scale mining in IP
areas; the prosecution of human rights violators in
IP communities; the respect for IPs´ rights to land
resources and self-determination; and the implementation
of international instruments on IP protection.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on NATIONAL CULTURAL COMMUNITIES since 2011-08-16
rows.remarks: Manifestation by Rep. Padilla. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.title_full: ON THE ISSUES SURROUNDING THE VICTORY OF THE PHILIPPINE DRAGON BOAT TEAM
rows.title_short: Absence Of Support And Recognition From The Philippine Government To The Philippine Dragon Boat Team
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the need for a congressional inquiry to determine the reasons why the government, particularly the Philippine Olympic Committee (POC) and the Philippine Sports Commission
(PSC), had failed to provide official recognition
to the Philippine Dragon Boat Federation Team
as a national team. Disclosed that the official
status as a national team and the corresponding benefits accruing therewith would have provided the Team with adequate budgetary support to help in their training preparations for international competitions. Claimed that the Team was able to surpass hardships and won five gold medals and two silver medals in the recently concluded 10th Annual World Dragon Boat Racing Championship in Tampa, Florida, USA.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-08-18
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Bagatsing and Ungab. Manifestation by Rep. Escudero. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-08-18
committee_action.meethigh: the committee urged the PSC, POC, PCKF and PDBF to hold a dialogue to thresh out the issues at hand. PDBF gave the assurance that they will attend the meeting scheduled next week by the PSC.

rows.author: E047
rows.title_short: Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program Extension With Reforms
rows.abstract:
Said that past and present land reform programs
failed because they protected the landlord instead of the farmer,... held that the two-year old Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program Extension with Reforms (CARPER) Law only worsened the anti-tenant and pro-landlord Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Law(CARL) and strengthened the monopoly of big landlords
in the agrarian sector. Cited statistics to
prove the government´s dismal land distribution record, pro-landlord bias in the modes of land transfer,and inadequate support services for farmers. Pointed out that land disputes in more than 13 estates and haciendas were not yet resolved; land conversion remained unabated; and the bulk of funds for land tenure improvement was spent for landowners´ compensation. Remarked that land reform under the Aquino Administration would not succeed if the rights and interests of tenants in the Aquino family´sHacienda Luisita were not protected and upheld. Said that HB No. 374 or the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill (GARB) was filed in the current Congress to achieve social justice, higher productivity and a better
quality of life, women empowerment, respect for
ancestral domain, and a stronger agricultural sector for overall progress and economic development.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-08-10)

rows.author: G092
rows.mother_status: Approved by the House on 2012-10-15, transmitted to on 2012-10-17 and received by the Senate on 2012-10-17
rows.title_full: FREE COLLEGE ENTRANCE EXAMINATIONS FOR HIGH SCHOOL STUDENTS
rows.abstract:
Focused on the entrance examination fees imposed by public and private colleges and universities,
which he believed had created an economic barrier that prevents public high school graduates from even applying for college.
Underscored that a standard national collegiate
examination would be enough..., but this should be administered free of charge by the State and should be prepared ... to make the system democratic and professional. Suggested that
any additional examination requirement should be given by the latter at its own expense, esp. since educational institutions enjoy very low tax rates with some of them even enjoying tax exemptions. Concluded that education should be accessible and affordable...a holistic school entrance examination system should be created to assess and assist prospective college students.
rows.status: Substituted by HB06577
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G099
rows.title_full: PROBLEMS OF OUR RIVER SYSTEMS (ALSO INTERGENERATIONAL RESPONSIBILITY)
rows.title_short: Marilao- Meycauyan- Obando- River System ( M M O R S )
rows.abstract:
Noted that both the Filipino´s identity and the country´s history are tied with the rivers. Appealed for the immediate rehabilitation
of the Marilao-Meycauyan-Obando-
River System (MMORS) which became heavily polluted due to the nonexistence of wastewater treatment facilities and domestic pollution. Disclosed that a 10-year rehabilitation plan intends to improve the water quality of MMORS even as she lauded the actions of LGUs and other
stakeholders in the protection of the river...
Underscored the importance of the immediate
implementation of the Valenzuela-Obando-
Meycauayan (VOM) flood control project.
Said that she had filed HB 4913 to help ensure that domestic wastes shall undergo treatment so as not to contaminate the environment.
Emphasized the importance of a two-pronged approach in addressing environmental degradation and solid waste management: congressional approval of the necessary budgetary allocation for the MMORS and the enlistment of support from public-private sector partnerships. Discussed the possibility of providing funds for certain infrastructure projects in the riverbanks,... Argued that a rehabilitated river system not only contributes to the environmental wellbeing of the affected locality but also paves the way for its ecological and economic development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ECOLOGY since 2011-10-04

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: THE ONGOING PEACE TALKS WITH CPP-NPA
rows.title_short: C P P - N P A
rows.abstract:
Initially focused on the members of the government panel,... Atty. Alex Padilla and Justice Sec. Leila de Lima, who were tasked with seeking peace with the CCP-NPA-NDF, and whom he
alleged have been misleading and misinforming the
people of their duty on representing the gov't. 
and ensuring a fair and just resolution to the Maoist terrorism and insurgency in the country. Cited as an example the release of the Morong 43 which he said had been described by legal pundits as a strong and loud slap against the rule of law and humanity. Opined that the government panel has been working with the NDF to advance their terrorist objectives, and cited certain instances of the 218 attacks made by NPA members against the government from January 1 to July 30, 2011,... Pointed out that said incidents happened during the initial peace talks in Norway, which showed the terrorist group´s insincerity to achieve peace. Observed the reluctance of the Commission on Human Rights to investigate glaring human rights violations, ...Called on Congress, through its appropriate committees, to conduct an investigation, ... to ferret out the truth on the wherewithal of the peace negotiations and to institute corrective measures, if necessary.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-10-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Bataoil. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G105
rows.abstract:
Argued on the reasons why the government´s conditional cash transfer (CCT) program is not only counterproductive but only further exploits the situation of poor Filipinos. Explained
that the main objective of the CCT...is negated by the failure of the government to regularize the CCT allocations to its beneficiaries and the subservience of the latter to intermittent dole-outs. Opined that the government´s CCT program is merely a superficial program to address short-term needs. Reasoned that empowering the poor and providing a permanent solution to their situation cannot be achieved through the continued implementation of the CCT or through funds provided through foreign aid. Claimed that what the marginalized
Filipinos need are realizable programs that will address their health, education, livelihood and employment problems, and their limited access to basic social services.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POVERTY ALLEVIATION since 2011-10-04

rows.author: G127
rows.title_full: PROPOSED CREATION OF A SUB-STATE IN MUSLIM MINDANAO
rows.title_short: Meeting Of Pres. Aquino Iii With M I L F Chairperson Al Hadj Murad.
rows.abstract: Spoke about the meeting of Pres. Benigno S. Aquino III with MILF Chairperson Al Hadj Murad. Expressed his reservations on the proposed creation of a substate in Muslim Mindanao which was being mentioned by the MILF in media. Suggested that Congress immediately 1) create a special ad hoc ctte. that would address the possible legalities that may come out of the current peace negotiations; 2) initiate consultations and dialogues with the concerned sectors; and 3) invite the members of the government negotiating panel to brief the Members on the mechanics of the process. Requested the Executive Branch to furnish Congress with a copy of the MILF´s so-called “Comprehensive Compact Agreement” as well as the draft of the government´s counter proposal. Enjoined the Senators to conduct parallel activities on their part.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on MUSLIM AFFAIRS since 2011-10-04

rows.author: F030
rows.title_full: AGRICULTURAL LANDS UNDER CARP IN THE 2ND DISTRICT OF SURIGAO DEL SUR
rows.title_short: Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program C A R P Beneficiaries
rows.abstract:
Related to the Body the case of the Pagmato farmers who had been cultivating private
agricultural lands in Sitio Towawog, Lingig, Surigao del Sur for a long period of time. Said that they were cheated of their rights as bona fide tenantfarmers when the government fraudulently acquired said lands through the voluntary offer to sell (VOS) scheme of the CARP and when certificates of land ownership award (CLOAs) and land titles were transferred to people who were not the prospective beneficiaries. Proposed for a conduct of a legislative inquiry into the anomalous transactions involving the fraudulent sale of agrarian lands in the guise of agrarian reform.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2011-10-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Garcia, P. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G118
rows.title_full: POVERTY SITUATION IN ILOILO
rows.title_short: Conditional Cash Transfer ( C C T )
rows.abstract:
Spoke on the implementation of the govt´s Poverty Alleviation Program specially the Pantawid Pampamilya Pilipino Program (4Ps)
under the conditional cash transfer (CCT) program in the Province of Iloilo. Mentioned certain issues and challenges that block the noble intention of said program to push the chronic poor out of the vicious cycle of poverty, to wit: 1) targeting system
of beneficiaries; 2) enough supply of the conditionalities; and 3) efficient monitoring of the program. Delved on the inefficiency of the CCT program in providing basic education and health care services to the beneficiaries upon interactions with the people of Iloilo.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POVERTY ALLEVIATION since 2011-10-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Magsaysay E. and Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: E022
rows.title_full: MAYUGA REPORT ON THE ALLEGED ELECTORAL FRAUD IN THE 2004 PRESIDENTIAL ELECTIONS
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body about the Mayuga Report which he claimed had been finally declassified and now open to public scrutiny. Maintained that the Mayuga Commission had been created to investigate
the so-called “Hello Garci scandal,” and the electoral fraud that happened in the 2004 elections.... Opined that the Mayuga Report was a “whitewash, a collection of vague statements, tentative findings, and weak recommendations, on the unprofessional conduct of the military officers and inadequate policy guidelines by the AFP. Underscored the vague recommendations of the Mayuga Commission to conduct further investigations to determine culpability and gave the several recommendation....Appealed to his colleagues to give justice to the victims of the 2004 cheating.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on SUFFRAGE AND ELECTORAL REFORMS since 2011-10-04

rows.title_full: COA AUDITOR'S REPORT ALLEGING IRREGULAR EXPENDITURES OF CONGRESSIONAL ALLOCATIONS
rows.abstract:
Talked about certain reports of the Commission on Audit (COA) re: utilization of her congressional allocation esp. on projects involving the DSWD and TESDA. Said that the COA opinion, which covered expenditures
that allegedly could be suspended or disallowed
in audit, could affect her character as a person and her conduct in public office. Said that it was clear that the COA lacked the moral expertise and sufficient knowledge about
programs and mechanics of implementation that are
emerging as unique and innovative. Requested that her speech be referred to the appropriate Committee, and thereafter appealed that an early hearing be scheduled and that COA Auditors
Cristina B. Briz and Noemi P. Wong, as well as the TESDA and DSWD officials concerned, be summoned to attend said hearing.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on APPROPRIATIONS since 2011-10-04

rows.title_short: Speech For Insertion Into The Records
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body that the trip of certain Members to Micronesia to attend the 76th Council Assembly of the Asian-Pacific Parliamentarians´ Union (APPU) and the 42nd APPU General Assembly which was scheduled from September 7 to 9, 2011 had been cancelled. Proposed that his speech be inserted into the Record of the House considering
that it involved the national interest (“Domestic legislation in aid of a rules-based approach in the West Philippine Sea”). Underscored that the only viable approach to settle disputes in the West Philippine Sea (WPS) involving the Spratly Islands is a rules-based approach which enjoins all parties to the dispute to (a) continue to respect and commit to
the principles of international law,particularly the 1982 United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS); (b) reiterate their commitment to resolve the disputes through peaceful means; and (c)recognize the need for a multilateral approach involving the claimant states and other legitimate stakeholders. Emphasized that the full and effective implementation of the ASEAN-China Declaration on the Conduct of Parties (DOC) in the South China Sea was imperative and would require an actionable framework. Pointed out that the concerned parties should consider the UNCLOS choices for dispute settlement and urged the Philippines to harmonize its
laws with the UNCLOS principles, citing in particular the bills establishing Phil. maritime zones and archipelagic sea lanes in Philippine waters.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-09-05)

rows.author: G052
rows.title_full: ISSUES ON THE MWSS AND ITS TWO CONCESSIONAIRES
rows.abstract:
Brought to the attention of the House the report... pertaining to the privatization by the MWSS of its water and sewerage facilities and services and which were transferred to two concessionaires, as well as the alleged violations of contractual obligations, statutory laws, and various legal and constitutional issues emanating therefrom. Underscored the immediate need to address these violations of law which resulted in: 1) graft and corruption in the MWSS; 2) wrongful interpretation that the two concessionaires, acting as mere agents of the MWSS, were considered as private utilities services and not as public utilities services as categorized in the Constitution; 3) anomalous transactions in the Regulatory Office (RO) which was created by the MWSS and funded by the two concessionaires; and 4) exemption of the two concessionaires from COA examination and audit. 
Advanced several recommendations which included among others: 1) the COA should start its legal and transaction audit of the MWSS concession system and the two concessionaires´ water
and sewerage utilities services; 2) the DOJ must undertake a review of the transactions of the MWSS-RO and should issue a ruling on whether or not the two concessionaires can be categorized as public utilities; 3) the COA and the
DOJ should issue a cease and desist order from the collection of payments from consumers after these bodies had determined the correct rates of payments; and 4) the COA or DOJ should order the concessionaires to refund excess charges to the consumers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on GOOD GOVERNMENT AND PUBLIC ACCOUNTABILITY since 2011-10-04
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Bello and Escudero. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: F095
rows.title_full: COLLECTION OF DUES FROM THE COOPERATIVE SECTOR BY THE NATIONAL ELECTRIFICATION ADMINISTRATION
rows.abstract:
Delved on the illegal collection being made by electric cooperatives registered with the
National Electrification Administration (NEA) of a certain amount charged in the electric bill of every consumer representing the member´s contribution for capital expenditures (MCC), without the knowledge of the consumers of the rationale behind the collection and where the proceeds of such collection go. Cited in particular the case of the Batangas Electric
Cooperative (Batelec) II. Enumerated his reasons for pushing for the registration of all electric cooperatives with the Cooperative Development Authority and proposed that the Body defer consideration of the proposed budgets of the Department of Energy, NEA and Energy Regulatory Commission if the subject matter of his speech was not resolved.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2011-10-04
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Ping-ay, Rivera, Batocabe, Cabaluna and Payoyo. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: A088
rows.title_full: COLLAPSE OF THE IRISAN DUMPSITE IN BAGUIO CITY CAUSED BY TYPHOON \"MINA\"
rows.abstract: Voiced his concern about the plight of Baguio City residents re: the continued operation of the Irisan dumpsite despite the clear prohibition thereof under the Ecological Waste Management Act of 20000. Said that the dumpsite caused several deaths when its retaining wall collpased in the wake of Typhoon Mina last August and should be used as a temporary garbage transfer area only, pending its development into a national park pursuant to the city's master plan. Explained the real reason behind its collapse, adding that Mayor Mauricio Domogan was not given the chance to ezxplain the same.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2011-11-15
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: G030
rows.title_full: BREAST CANCER AWARENESS MONTH
rows.abstract:
Raised the issue of breast cancer in view of the worldwide celebration of Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Cited statistics on increasing breast cancer cases and enumerated World Health Organization (WHO) detection recommendations such as selfbreast examination and mammography.
Discussed the physical and financial difficulties suffered by breast cancer patients. Mentioned the pilot program of the DOH on providing medicine for early-stage breast cancer as well as House legislators´ breast cancer awareness and prevention program,... Asked the Department to provide cheaper medicines and
conduct more information campaigns. Urged the Body to push for the adoption of a national health agenda for breast cancer and the
expansion of said DOH program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2011-11-15

rows.author: G092
rows.title_full: QUESTIONABLE SUSPENSION OF IMPLEMENTATION OF PROJECTS IN TAGUIG
rows.abstract:
Cited incidents in Taguig City where the local government blocked the implementation of infrastructure projects of the national government as well as of private individuals.  Stressed that he supported the devolution of local governments but that a check and-
balance system must be in place to ensure
responsible governance.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC WORKS AND HIGHWAYS since 2011-11-15

rows.author: F102
rows.title_full: PLIGHT OF THE PAL EMPLOYEES ASSOCIATION (PALEA) MEMBERS
rows.title_short: Philippine Airline's ( P A L ' S ) Outsourcing Plan
rows.abstract:
Pointed out the PAL management´s contravention of its agreement with the PALEA by proceeding with its outsourcing plan even before the September 30, 2011 deadline thereby resulting in the early termination of PALEA workers. Asked the Members to look into, among others, the plight of the PALEA workers and determine the responsibility and accountability of the PAL management over the events which led to the September 27 protest action of PALEA members, the justification behind PAL´s “spin-off” plan allegedly due to financial losses, the risk to the physical safety of PAL passengers by management´s hiring of unqualified workers, and the adverse effects on the economy of PAL´s practice of labor contractualization. Expressed his appeal to the Body to initiate a congressional inquiry into the PAL management´s wanton disregard for workers´ rights, its hiring of unqualified workers to perform tasks that require a certain level of knowledge and competency thereby compromising the physical safety of the passengers of PAL as well as the airlines´ overall operations, and the complicity of the police and private security forces
in the dispersal of PAL workers.
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-10-18
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Romualdo, Remulla and Lagman. Referred to the appropriate committee.

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-10-18

rows.author: F104
rows.abstract:
Defended the right of the Filipino youth to
participate in political activities,...arguing that speaking and acting decisively on socio-political issues are part of the youth´s learning process as well as essential components
of civic education in a democracy. Disagreed with the contrary position held by Malacañang
officials to the successful staging recently
of a nationwide strike by teachers and students to 1)protest the budget cuts and insufficient funding of State universities and colleges (SUCs), 2) demand the realignment of the 2012 Budget Bill to allow more funds for the improvement of public higher education, and 3) urge the Aquino Administration to review its higher education policy. Opined that the Aquino
government should even be thankful to the youth for their efforts in fighting for a better future and concluded that the social policies of the Aquino Administration nourish the ground for critical dissent and that the insensitivity of its officials forces the people to struggle for their basic rights.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-09-26)
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Marcoleta and Escudero. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F086
rows.title_full: CALLED FOR THE REEXAMINATION OF THE AIRLINE CABOTAGE LAWS
rows.abstract:
Took to task certain airline companies for their failure to deliver prompt and reliable services
to airline passengers, which he deemed to be a
violation of their legislative franchises to operate in the service of passengers. Informed the Body about his personal experiences with these airlines to emphasize the plight of airline passengers whose flights sometimes get delayed or cancelled without sufficient advisories or notices from the airline companies.
Underscored the standard reply of these airlines to these inconveniences and claimed that the affected passengers deserve better services
than the token “sorry for the inconvenience” excuses. Urged Congress to review the legislated certificates of public convenience and franchises of airline companies and to look into
the possibility of lifting airline cabotage laws to promote competition in the airline industry.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on TRANSPORTATION since 2011-11-15

rows.author: F103
rows.title_full: IMPACT OF TYPHOONS \"PEDRING\" AND \"QUIEL\" TO AGRICULTURE
rows.title_short: Government's Slow Response To Natural Disasters
rows.abstract:
Delved on the sad state of Philippine agriculture and the government´s seeming helplessness to respond effectively to the devastation brought by natural calamities as experienced by the country recently with Typhoons Pedring and Quiel which was similar to the destruction caused by Typhoon Ondoy two years ago. Voiced the following concerns whenever the country is hit by natural calamities
especially typhoons: 1) the damages caused
to the country specifically to the agriculture and fisheries sectors; 2) the proper protocol to be followed when releasing water from dams; and 3) the absence of adequate means to protect the farmers against calamities. Recommended, among
others, that the Department of Agriculture (DA) restock and redistribute certified seeds and other agricultural inputs to farmers affected by floods and immediately release funds to affected farmers and fisherfolk for production assistance; that the National Food Authority (NFA) procure wet palay from small farmers to help them recover part of their lost incomes;
and that the President immediately issue a
moratorium on the conversion of agricultural lands. Stressed the need for leaders to
point the way forward and to assure the people that the government will help them.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRICULTURE AND FOOD since 2011-11-15

rows.author: E047
rows.title_short: Rights Of Farmers Of Hacienda Looc, Nasugbu, Batangas
rows.abstract:
Spoke in Filipino about the 15-year old struggle
of farmers in Hacienda Looc in Nasugbu, Batangas
against land grabbing, land conversion, and environmental destruction -- all for the sake of eco-tourism. Pointed out that the hacienda was strategically located, had a huge business potential, and was blessed with rich resources.
Traced how agrarian reform beneficiaries lost
emancipation patents, certificates of land ownership award and certificates of land transfer when the government illegally and anomalously sold the hacienda including those portions covered by land reform under PD No. 27 and the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program. Described how real estate firms such as SM Land, Inc. deceived residents and farmers to give up their lands in return for development and modernization, or harassed and violently ejected them with the help of military and police forces.
Stressed that the farmers of Hacienda Looc would not give up their rights despite a President who was himself a hacendero and whose policies, the former alleged, were more protourism and probusiness than profarmer.
rows.status: Pending First Reading (Filed last 2011-10-04)

rows.author: G032
rows.title_full: IMPORTANCE OF CRAFTING NEW HEALTH POLICIES
rows.abstract:
Informing his colleagues about his personal
battle with cancer,... spoke on the issue of health and well-being of the people which he
deemed as the most important aspect of human development. Gave an overview of cancer incidents
and other deadly diseases in the Philippines, lamented the pitiful state of the country´s public health care system due to inadequate public health personnel and government budget, and expressed support to government´s initiatives, such as expanding the coverage
and enhancement of benefit delivery of Phil-
Health, improving access to upgraded, quality hospitals and health care facilities through the Health Facility Enhancement Program (HFEP) and attaining health-related Millennium Development Goals (MDGs). Sought the support of his
colleagues to create more significant laws and initiate programs that are beneficial to the health and wellbeing of the people and underscored that health should be their main concern as it is a good investment for nation-building.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2011-11-15

rows.author: G093
rows.title_full: COMMEMORATION OF WORLD TEACHERS DAY
rows.abstract:
Spoke in observance of World Teachers Day on the plight of public school teachers specifically with regard to their appeal for an increase in their salary or the so called “chalk allowance,” their security of tenure and just working conditions, the regularization of volunteer
and contractual teachers, the increase in classrooms and other school facilities, and the prescription of the policy of precarious employment in the education sector.
As Pres. Aquino had shown appreciation for
the efforts of public school teachers and considering that gov't employees would soon receive the final installment of the salary increases ..., Rep. Tinio called on the Members to begin to study and deliberate on the new round of salary increases for government employees starting in 2013 to give honor and what is due to public school teachers.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on BASIC EDUCATION AND CULTURE since 2011-11-15

rows.author: G044
rows.title_full: ENERGY SITUATION IN MINDANAO
rows.title_short: Construction Of Solar Power Plants In Mindanao
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body about a serious electric power problem in Mindanao if the Department of Energy (DOE) would not immediately implement under its National Renewable Energy Program the construction of an initial capacity of 235
megawatts of solar photovoltaic power plants by
2015. Enumerated several courses of action
for the pertinent government agencies to address
the development of renewable energy in the country including, among others: 1) the allocation by the DOE of 100 MW to be generated from solar photovoltaic power plants; 2) the immediate resolution and decision by the ERC on hearings regarding feed-in tariff petition before the end of 2011; and 3) the conduct
of a congressional inquiry on the reasons why
the DOE had reduced to only 50 MW the required
initial generation output from solar photovoltaic
power plants. Informed the Body that he had
filed House Resolution No. 1758 to address several of these recommendations and another resolution to specifically inquire into the tepid support of the DOE to the National Renewable Energy Program.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2011-11-15
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Golez R., Rodriguez, R. and Romualdo. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: G012
rows.title_full: CONTINUING NPA ATTACKS AMIDST THE ONGOING PEACE PROCESS
rows.abstract:
Condemned the continuing attacks by the New People´s Army (NPA) against business
establishments, public facilities, military and police personnel, foreigners and ordinary citizens despite its ongoing peace negotiation with the national government. Cited in particular the recent burning in Tarlac
province of 12 buses and a truck owned by Victory
Liner, Inc.,... Mentionedthe previous day´s headline of the Philippine Daily Inquirer on the three mines hit by NPA guerillas in Claver, Surigao del Norte where three security guards were killed, and enumerated other NPA atrocities in areas like Tagum, Surigao, Masbate, Catanduanes, Compostela Valley and Quezon. Disclosed that the Provincial Bus Operators Association of the Philippines, as well as Malacañang, have condemned the burning of buses and the NPA´s acts of violence and asked his colleagues to study the country´s policies and directives regarding the matter...
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-11-15

rows.author: G120
rows.title_full: ENVIRONMENTAL DEGRADATION OF LAKE LANAO AND ITS IMPACT ON THE MINDANAO POWER CRISIS
rows.abstract:
Focused on the Mindanao power crisis that was addressed by former Energy Secretary Angelo Reyes through the procurement of oil-fed generators which, he claimed, was only a
temporary solution. Stressed that the root of the
crisis could be attributed to the more serious environmental problem of the diminishing water inflow to Lake Lanao due to the destruction of its watershed compounded by the impact of climate change. Informed his colleagues about the importance of Lake Lanao to national development and the various laws which were enacted to manage and protect the lake but which the mandated agencies had neglected to enforce effectively to prevent the environmental
degradation of Lake Lanao and to address
the socio-economic rehabilitation of the people and communities affected by the impact of damming the Lake. Proposed the enactment of a law
creating the Ranao Development Authority (RDA)
which would require no additional government expenses but only the realignment of the resources already provided for under the Local Government Code of 1991 and the Electric Power Industry Reform Act.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on ENERGY since 2011-11-15

rows.title_full: MISUSE OF PDAF GIVEN TO THE PHILIPPINE GENERAL HOSPITAL
rows.title_short: Unexplained Use Of His Medical Assistance Fund In Philippine General Hospital
rows.abstract:
Informed the Body about a scam allegedly perpetuated by some personnel of the accounting
and pharmacy departments of the Philippine
General Hospital (PGH) who had misused his Priority Development Assistance Fund (PDAF) which he has been allocating to the PGH to meet the health and medical needs of indigent patients from his district. Called for a congressional investigation on said anomaly and proposed that PGH Director Dr. Jose Gonzales and his cohorts be meted a temporary preventive
suspension order. Advised his colleagues
to check on their respective PDAF allocations
in the different public hospitals to determine
any anomaly in the use of these funds.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on HEALTH since 2011-11-15
rows.remarks: Reps Fua's and Romualdo's amendment to Rep. Bagatsing's motion. Manifestations by Reps. Crisologo, Kho (D.), Padilla and Escudero. Interpellations by Reps. Crisologo and Tugna. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: F099
rows.title_full: STATE OF COOPERATIVES IN THE PHILIPPINES
rows.abstract:
Spoke about the state of cooperatives in the country. Claimed that there are about 20,000 cooperatives with about seven million members comprising of farmers, fisherfolk, farmers, teachers, and representatives of the marginalized
sectors of the society, who had chosen to build
a better life for themselves and their families through cooperatives. Informed the Body that the country´s cooperatives are recognized for their significant contributions to the country´s development. Stressed the social, labor, and economic impact of cooperatives in society. Relayed its clamor for the conversion of the CDA into a fullfledged department in order to enhance its services; and for the continued compliance by government agencies and LGUs, with
the tax exemption privilege granted it by RA No. 6938 and 9520. Said that the sector aimed to become an indispensable component of national
development by strengthening cooperatives in
the agrarian and agricultural sector; building consultation, advocacy, and feedback structures and systems; and establishing links with business and other sectors. Asked the legislature to provide a legislative
framework conductive to cooperative growth and
development.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2011-11-15
rows.remarks: Interpellations by Reps. Romualdo, Biazon, Golez (R.) and Fua. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: C128
rows.title_full: COOPERATIVES IN WATER DISTRICTS
rows.abstract: Rep. Cresente C. Paez expressed support to the promotion of water cooperatives and the strengthening of the water districts by proposing the conversion of the latter from GOCC into consumer-owned cooperatives for eventual transfer to the members consumers;... discussed the case of the Cagayan de Oro Water District (COWD) whose alleged inefficiencies and transparency issues prompted the consumers to form and register the Water Consumers Cooperative (WATERCOOP)with the CDA,...; underscored the reasons behind the proposal of Party-List Coop-NATCCO to convert water districts into cooperatives and thereafter proposed that Congress should amend the Provincial Water Utilities Act of 1973 and the Water Code of the Philippines. As water districts should be subject to the principles of accountability, transparency and regulatory effectiveness, he expressed hope that their recommendations would be considered along the thrust of the President´s declaration regarding the creation of a water super body that will oversee and manage the country´s water supply.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2011-11-15

rows.author: G122
rows.title_full: COOPERATIVES IN THE BANKING INDUSTRY
rows.abstract:
Rep. Lico underscored ...several matters which justify the need for government´s recognition
of the significance of cooperative banks by
granting them more privileges. He stated that among the significant developments and reforms which he and his colleagues in the cooperative sector have achieved in Congress include :
1) the creation of the Strengthening
Program under which cooperative banks are given
additional period of time to gain back their solvency through the guidance and assistance of financial institutions like the Land Bank, the DBP and the PDIC; and 2) Reps. Ping-ay
and Paez´ filing of H.B.No. 4478 or the proposed
“Cooperative Banking Act” governing the operations of cooperative banks. He enjoined the Members to support the Bill as the cooperative banking sector badly needs the help of Congress to keep the spirit of cooperativism alive.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2011-11-15

rows.author: F103
rows.title_full: STATE OF AGRICULTURE COOPERATIVES AND AGRARIAN REFORM
rows.title_short: Activities For The Cooperative Month Celebration
rows.abstract:
Rep. Agapito H. Guanlao... stated that the CDA is
spearheading the country´s preparation for the
launching of the International Year of Cooperatives (IYC) in 2012 which he deemed as significant in view of the recognition which cooperatives justly deserve. He thereafter traced the historical development
of cooperatives in the Philippines and the
movements they have spawned in ending poverty and
bring about societal change among Filipinos; cited the laws that were enacted focusing on rural organizations and the provision of financial assistance therefore; emphasized how the cooperative movement has continued to gain strength through its membership and assets; and underscored the contributions of cooperatives as economic entities and selfhelp organizations.
... recommended that Congress should strengthen credit guarantee mechanisms and pass measures to support the cooperative movement in general.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2011-11-15

rows.author: G117
rows.title_full: CONVERSION OF ELECTRIC COOPERATIVES
rows.abstract:
Rep. Payuyo spoke on the various issues impinging
on the status of electric cooperatives and the goal of bringing complete and genuine consumer ownership of said cooperatives, which included, among others, the functions and powers of the NEA regarding the supervision and control of electric cooperatives, the culture of corruption prevailing in the electric cooperative sector as borne out in a World Bank study on NEA´s operations, and the proposed reforms under the EPIRA.  Rep. Payuyo expressed his appeal to the Members to assist their constituents regarding the proposed referendum on the question of registration of electric cooperatives with the CDA, and for the NEA not to hinder this effort. Likewise, he recommended that the Department of Energy (DOE) exercise decisive leadership to allow electric cooperatives to benefit from privatization and to protect them from the domination of cartels.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on COOPERATIVES DEVELOPMENT since 2011-11-15
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Rep. Ledesma. Referred to the appropriate committee.

rows.author: B020
rows.title_full: CASE OF MAYOR YAP OF ESCALANTE, NEGROS OCCIDENTAL
rows.abstract:
Rep. Ledesma dwelt on a resolution issued by the
Napolcom suspending the administrative and operational control of Escalante Mayor Melecio Yap over the Escalante police station for his alleged involvement in extrajudicial killings in Escalante City and the First District of
Negros Occidental; stressed that despite several
requests, the DILG and Napolcom had not presented
any documentary evidence that would support
the allegation; pointed out that since the Napolcom started its investigation, it never sought his position on said resolution; stressed that a statement in the resolution that the Commission did not receive any recommendation from him despite several attempts to get his comments, was inaccurate.
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on LOCAL GOVERNMENT since 2011-11-15

rows.author: G107
rows.title_full: CELEBRATION OF ELDERLY WEEK
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE OF REP. KHO (D.)
Recognized by the Chair, Representative
David L. Kho from Party-List Coalition of Senior
Citizens in the Philippines Inc. spoke, in
celebration of the International Week of the
Elderly or Linggo ng Nakatatanda, about the
senior citizens exclusive club which comprises
seven million members who are educated,
dedicated and well-experienced in their various
advocacies and interest. He then focused his
speech on the strict implementation of Republic
Act No. 9994 such as: the putting up of senior
citizens´ centers nationwide; establishment of
livelihood training programs; medical and
financial assistance to indigent senior citizens and their mandatory PhilHealth coverage; social
enhancement and additional social pension
coverage; and information and awareness drive on
the rights of senior citizens. He thereafter disclosed that at least two of the more than a dozen bills they have sponsored have passed the committee level and subsequently sought the support of the Members on a bill which they have filed in partnership with the University of the Philippines Philippine General Hospital (UP
PGH), seeking the establishment of an institute on aging research and development knowledge for
senior citizens.
(Source: JOURNAL NO. 22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on POPULATION AND FAMILY RELATIONS since 2011-11-15

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: EFFECTS TO THE ECONOMY OF THE VIOLENT ATTACKS ALLEGEDLY PERPETRATED BY THE CPP-NDF-NPA
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE OF REP. ALCOVER
Recognized by the Chair on motion of Rep. Fariñas, Rep. Pastor M. Alcover Jr. of Party-List
ANAD took the floor and spoke about the recent
violent acts perpetuated by the country´s communist rebels against businesses and innocent civilians as criticized by the international human rights watchdog Human Rights Watch and United Nations rapporteur Philip Alston. He then inquired what concerned government agencies, such as the Department of Justice (DOJ), the Commission on Human Rights (CHR), and particularly the Office of the President (OP) have been doing to correct the rebels´ propaganda that the government alone is responsible for the many extrajudicial killings.
Rep. Alcover also criticized the ineptitude of
the Aquino presidency in addressing the negative
economic consequences of the rebels´ latest acts of violence as well as in taking full responsibility for what the government considered as “security lapses.” In this regard, he asked his colleagues to unite and make an urgent appeal for the President´s
decisive action on the matter.
(Source JOURNAL NO. 22)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PUBLIC ORDER AND SAFETY since 2011-11-15

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: LABOR OUTSOURCING PROGRAM INITIATED BY PHILIPPINE AIRLINES
rows.title_short: Phil. Airlines Employee's Fight Against  D O L E Decision
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGEOF REP. MARIANO
Upon recognition by the Chair, Rep. Rafael V.
Mariano of Party-List Anakpawis tackled in
Filipino the continuing labor dispute involving the Philippine Airlines (PAL) in light of the recent implementation of PAL management´s outsourcing plan that caused the dismissal of thousands of PAL employees. He also referred to the Supreme Court´s recent dismissal of the case filed by the Flight Attendants and Stewardess Association of the Philippines against PAL management, as well as the Court of Appeal´s decision to reopen the P730 million damage
suit filed by PAL against the pilots who went
on strike in 1998 to protest unfair labor practices against the company; lamented that the courts, the Department of Labor and Employment, and even Malacañang have all made favorable decisions for PAL, thus emboldening it to make actions that are detrimental to the welfare of the employees. He said that despite their situation, the PAL employees have continued to pursue their cause, and asked that his speech be immediately referred to the Committee on Labor and Employment.
(Source Journal No. 22)
rows.status: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-10-18

committee_action.action: Under deliberation by the Mother Committee on 2011-10-18

rows.author: F093
rows.title_full: IN COMMEMORATION OF THE BATASAN BOMBING
rows.title_short: Anniversary Of House Of Representatives' Bombing
rows.abstract:
Recognized by the Chair upon Rep. Banal´s motion,
Rep. Luzviminda C. Ilagan from Party-List
Gabriela pointed out that the day marked the fourth anniversary of the bombing of the House of Representatives which resulted in death and injury to office workers as well as Members of the House including her and Reps. Pryde Henry A. Teves and Wahab Akbar. She said that the emotional scars of the victims and their families remained because the perpetrators
of and motive behind the crime still had to be identified and justice still had to be attained. She asked her colleagues to act on a House Resolution which she and Rep. Teves had filed, for the installation of a plaque containing the names of the victims in the South Wing Lobby in commemoration of the incident.
(House Journal No. 23, p.14)

rows.author: A010
rows.title_full: ON CONSTITUTIONALITY OF THE CREATION OF THE PROVINCE OF DINAGAT ISLANDS
rows.title_short: Delayed Benefits For The People Of Dinagat Island
rows.abstract:
Rep. Aumentado spoke with reservation in support
of the plight of the people of Dinagat Province
who have been suffering from the adverse effects of the delay in the resolution of 1) a pending motion for reconsideration filed by the petitioners in the case declaring Republic Act No. 9355 or the creation of Dinagat Province as unconstitutional; and 2) another case convicting Rep. Ruben B. Ecleo Jr. for alleged violation of the Anti-Graft and Corrupt Practices Act while he was the town mayor of San Jose, thereby
depriving said province representation in the House of Representatives. He disclosed that due to the delayed action of the Supreme Court on the two cases, the province has been continuously deprived of its share in the internal revenue allotment thus hampering the delivery of basic services to the people and depriving its people representation in Congress. He concluded that the speedy disposition of these cases was paramount in the administration of justice.
(House Journal No. 23, p.16)

rows.author: F118
rows.title_full: ON ALLEGED COLLUSION BETWEEN LEADERS OF THE GOVERNMENT AND MEMBERS OF THE CPP-NPA
rows.title_short: Peace Talks Between The Philippine Government And The Rebels
rows.abstract:
Rep. Alcover underscored what he perceived to
be a vacillating attitude of the national leadership in dealing with local insurgents as he cited 1) several instances of murderous attacks made by elements of the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) and the Communist Party of the Philippines-New People´s Army (CPP-NPA) against the military in several parts of Mindanao; 2) the public statements of President
Benigno S. Aquino III, specifically those rebuking military officers for the loss of lives of civilians and soldiers in the most recent MILF attacks and his resolve to continue the government´s peace negotiations with the MILF leaders; and 3) the decision of the Aquino Administration to provide huge government
funds for capability-building purposes to the
MILF and a breakaway communist group leadership,
allegedly to honor the previous commitments of
President Aquino´s predecessors. He asked why the Administration was negotiating peace with the NPA whom it acknowledged to be extortionists and emphasized that any peace agreement with and government financial assistance to the CPP-NPA would only be used in furthering the latter´s
socio-political and military agenda. He then
stressed the position of ANAD Party-List that the
peace process must be righteous and fair and the
signing of a final peace agreement should be followed by disarmament, demobilization and reintegration. He subsequently asked top officials to act on reports that a clique was buying peace in return for the President´s political ambition, and urged Congress to
investigate the status of the peace negotiations with various rebel groups. 
(House Journal No. 23,pp.16-17)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on PEACE, RECONCILIATION AND UNITY since 2011-11-22
rows.remarks: Interpellation by Reps. Fua and Biazon. Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: E047
rows.title_full: ON AGRARIAN REFORM ISSUES IN HACIENDA LUISITA AND THE NEED TO PASS HB 374 (INSTITUTING GENUINE AGRARIAN REFORM IN THE COUNTRY)
rows.abstract:
QUESTION OF PRIVILEGE OF REP. MARIANO
Speaking in Filipino, Rep. Mariano delved on the
plight of the farmers and farmworkers in the Aquino-owned Hacienda Luisita and their continuing struggle for genuine land reform, together with the rest of the country´s peasantry, seven years after the massacre of
several farmers in the plantation. He said that to date, no one has yet been charged, jailed or punished for the crime. He informed the Body of what he considered as the seven grave sins of the Cojuangco-Aquino family against the interest of the farmer-beneficiaries in Hacienda
Luisita among which were the exemption of
Hacienda Luisita from the coverage of the Comprehensive Agrarian Reform Program (CARP) and the so-called compromise agreement allowing the farmers to choose between land or stock ownership under the stock distribution option (SDO). He also lamented that land grabbing, extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, harassment and oppression ofthe farmers still continue in the different parts of the country. In light of the foregoing, he enjoined the
Members to give justice to the victims of the Hacienda Luisita massacre and to approve House Bill No. 374 or the Genuine Agrarian Reform Bill in order to promote the interest of the farmers.
(House Journal No. 25, p.15)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on AGRARIAN REFORM since 2011-11-22
rows.remarks: Referred to the Committee on Rules.

rows.author: C032
rows.title_full: IN COMMEMORATION OF THE 22ND ANNIVERSARY OF THE ADOPTION OF THE UNITED NATION CONVENTION ON THE RIGHTS OF THE CHILD (UNCROC)
rows.title_short: United Nation's Convention On The Rights Of The Child
rows.abstract:
Rep. Cerilles spoke about the commemoration of
the 22nd anniversary of the United Nations
Convention on the Rights of the Child (UNCRC) for
which an exhibit of photographs depicting the core principles of the Convention was being held at the North Wing lobby of the House of Representatives main building with the participation of the Child Rights Network (CRN), the Philippine NGO Coalition on the UNCRC, and the House Committee on the Welfare of Children.
Furthermore, she disclosed that the Committee
Affairs Department of the House has spearheaded the development of the children´s checklist as a tool guide for assessing the compliance of proposed measures with the UNCRC, which was launched earlier that day. She added that Deputy Speaker Climaco and Minority Leader Edcel C. Lagman had filed House Resolution No. 1902 which seeks the utilization of a children´s checklist in the legislative process thus ensuring a human rights-based approach to policymaking. Rep. Cerilles thereafter expressed her gratitude to
the Members of the House for their help in the
approval on Third Reading of several measures that will protect Filipino children from homelessness, violence and exploitation. She further sought the help of the Committee on Appropriations and the Members of the House to enact into law the Special Education Bill and provide for the necessary appropriations to create special education centers for children with special needs.
(House Jornal No. 26, pp.4-5)
rows.status: Pending with the Committee on WELFARE OF CHILDREN since 2011-11-29

rows.author: G052
rows.title_full: ON THE COUNTRY'S COMMITMENT TO THE UNCROC
rows.title_short: Honoring The Stipulations Of The U N Convention On The Rights Of The Child
rows.abstract:
Rep. Herrera-Dy underscored the significance of
the UNCRC which also forms part of the law of the
land as well as the importance of the full
implementation of the laws that Congress had
enacted to conform to the country´s ratification of the Convention.She stressed that in pinciple, the UNCRC fundamentally provides for the best interests and rights of children to life, survival and development, nondiscrimination, and to participate in all important socio-political processes affecting their welfare. Rep. Herrera-Dy thereafter pointed out that the laws that Congress had passed to protect the rights of
children and juveniles from enforced labor and
employment, discrimination in social status, physical and psychological violence, sexual exploitation and the lack of legal protection, had been complemented by the creation of the Committee on Welfare of Children in the 14th Congress and the proposal to create an Ombudsman for Children to ensure the protection of their rights under the law. She then appealed to her colleagues not to rest on these legislative accomplishments, but rather work on the more comprehensive legislative undertakings that
will serve the best interest of the Filipino child.
